Story.Title: Survival in Valles Marineris on Mars
Story.Plot: You are members of an advanced colony crew heading toward the main dome of the "Ares-1" base on Mars. During descent, your cargo rover was hit by a violent dust storm and flipped over 150 kilometers away from your destination. The rover's life support systems are down, and communications with the base are cut off. Your objective: travel 150 km across the Martian desert to reach the base. You are wearing spacesuits, but resources are limited.

Evaluations.Rank: EXCELLENT. Elon Musk would be proud of you. You are the elite of space colonization!
GOOD. You will make it to the base, though with some minor frostbite.
ACCEPTABLE. You will probably get stuck halfway with dead batteries.
POOR. This indicates relying too heavily on Earth-bound logic.
DISASTER. You have become part of the Martian landscape. Your remains will serve as fertilizer.

Item.Name: Compressed oxygen tanks
Item.Description: The most critical item of all. The Martian atmosphere is unbreathable. Without oxygen, death is immediate.

Item.Name: Thermal generator (RTG)
Item.Description: Essential to prevent freezing. Mars is extremely cold (down to -60°C). This device provides constant heat for you and your suits.

Item.Name: Navigation unit (Gyroscope)
Item.Description: Your electronic compass. There are no GPS satellites on Mars. Without this tool, you would get lost in the desert instantly.

Item.Name: Water supply (20 liters)
Item.Description: Essential for life. Walking 150 kilometers requires massive physical effort, and you will need water for several days of travel.

Item.Name: Liquid sealant spray
Item.Description: A "band-aid" for spacesuits. If your suit scratches or punctures against sharp rocks, this fluid seals the hole instantly.

Item.Name: High-calorie protein paste tubes
Item.Description: Nutritious food that is light to carry. It will provide the energy needed for the estimated 3 to 5 days of walking.

Item.Name: Airtight inflatable tent
Item.Description: A small mobile shelter. It allows you to create a safe air bubble to take off your suit, eat, and rest.

Item.Name: Flexible solar panels
Item.Description: Useful for recharging suit systems during the day, although dust kicked up by the storm will reduce their efficiency.

Item.Name: First aid kit
Item.Description: Standard medicines and bandages. Necessary to treat cuts, wounds, or minor injuries that might occur during the trek.

Item.Name: Kevlar rope (30m)
Item.Description: Very strong and lightweight. Used to overcome slopes, climb down canyons, or tie yourselves together so you don't get lost if visibility drops.

Item.Name: Titanium folding shovel
Item.Description: A practical tool. After dust storms, it will be highly useful to shovel away sand and clear out shelter entrances or base airlocks.

Item.Name: Powerful laser pointer
Item.Description: An excellent visual signaling device. The light beam can be seen very far in the thin Martian air. Useful to get noticed by rescue teams.

Item.Name: Compressed nitrogen tank
Item.Description: Nearly useless. It is unbreathable, and the tank's pressure is too weak to push or move a person on the surface.

Item.Name: Magnetic compass
Item.Description: Useless. Mars lacks a global magnetic field like Earth, so the compass needle will just spin aimlessly without showing any direction.

Item.Name: Plasma lighter
Item.Description: Useless. The Martian atmosphere consists of carbon dioxide and lacks oxygen. Lighting a fire or flame is physically impossible.
